name: Noms API
description:
**Noms** is a REST API for nutritional data: **foods**, **brands**, **nutrients**
and **food groups**.

## Authentication

Send your API key in the `X-API-Key` header on every `/v1` request:

```
X-API-Key: noms_sk_...
```

## Responses

- **Envelope.** Every response is wrapped as `{ "data": … }`. List responses also
  carry `links` (pagination URLs) and `meta` (page info).
- **Types.** Keys are `snake_case`, timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC (`...Z`), and decimals
  are JSON **strings** to keep full precision (e.g. `"12.5000"`, never a rounded
  float).

## Querying lists

- **Pagination.** Set a page size with `page_size`, then follow `links.next` until
  `meta.has_more` is `false`. A cursor stays valid as the catalog changes underneath
  it, so a page you fetch is never invalidated by one you have not fetched yet. If you
  sort on a value that can change (a nutrient, a brand name), a row whose value moves
  while you are paging can repeat or be missed — de-duplicate by `id`, and walk the
  whole catalog on the default `id` order, which never moves.
- **Filtering.** `?name[eq]=Milk` (a bare `?name=Milk` defaults to `eq`); operators
  are `eq`, `in`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte` where the field supports them. Filters
  match only rows with a present value: on a nullable field, `[eq]=false` (or any
  comparison) excludes `null` rows. For example, `is_foundational[eq]=false`
  returns explicitly-`false` foods, not the undetermined (`null`) ones.
- **Sorting.** `?sort=name` (ascending) or `?sort=-name` (descending); comma-join
  for tie-breakers.
- **Text search.** `?q=...` is typo-tolerant — a close-but-misspelled word still
  finds the right food. With no explicit `sort`, results come back best match
  first. A `sort` given *alongside* `q` breaks ties within that ordering rather
  than replacing it — to order strictly by a column, omit `q`.
- **Sorting by nutrient.** `?sort=-nutrient[PROTEIN]` orders foods by their
  per-100 g/ml value for a nutrient code. Foods that do not carry the nutrient
  rank **last** rather than being dropped, so the result count is the same as
  the unsorted query's.
- **Sorting by brand.** `?sort=brand_name` orders by the food's brand; unbranded
  foods rank last, on the same rule.
- **Sparse fieldsets.** Return only the keys you need with `fields[<resource>]`, e.g.
  `?fields[foods]=id,name`.
- **Includes.** `/v1/foods` can embed related resources with `include=`, e.g.
  `include=brand,food_group,nutrients,serving_sizes,images,market_countries`.

## Errors

Every error is an **RFC 9457** problem document served as `application/problem+json`,
with a stable `type`, a human-readable `title` and `detail`, the HTTP `status`, and
resource-specific extension members where useful.

## Rate limits

Your account has a request quota for its plan, and every key you hold draws on the same
allowance — a second key never buys a second quota. The window is a rolling 24 hours on
the free plan and your billing period on the paid plans.
Every `/v1` resource response carries `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, and
`RateLimit-Reset` headers (plus legacy `X-RateLimit-*` aliases) so you can see where
you stand before hitting the wall. Once the quota is exhausted, requests return
**`429 Too Many Requests`** (an RFC 9457 problem) with a `Retry-After` header. Wait
until the window resets, then retry.

## Free-tier limits

The free tier is built for **looking things up**, not bulk-downloading the dataset:

- **Search or fetch by id.** List endpoints require a `?q=` search; a bare or
  filter-only list returns **`403`** (`/problems/enumeration-forbidden`). Any single
  record is always reachable with `GET /v1/{resource}/{id}`.
- **Result depth.** Search results are capped at roughly the first **1,000** matches;
  paging past that returns **`403`** (`/problems/result-depth-exceeded`).
- **Single market.** The free tier serves **one** market (country). Choose it in the
  dashboard or with `PUT /v1/market`; until you do, `foods` requests return **`403`**
  (`/problems/market-not-selected`). After that, `foods` is scoped to that market. The
  choice belongs to your **account**, so every key you hold shares it.

Paid tiers lift all three: full enumeration, unlimited pagination depth, all markets.
